title: M4 first increment: inert durable executor journal and bounded production store
outcome: Implement the smallest independently landable M4 foundation: versioned executor journal and bounded deduplicating production store APIs, carrying the frozen seven-test prep onto the current M2+M3 candidate. Source-only authorization from Fable2 #669; all builds/tests remain held. No network or runtime executor is enabled, and the parent remains incomplete.
acceptance: The production coordination schema adds a versioned executor journal on the accepted M2+M3 schema, upgrades historical v2 databases without changing mailbox messages, issued receipts or cursors, and preserves M3 delivery intents, deduplication and wake obligations. The seven frozen federation_m4_journal_ prerequisite tests pass unchanged, with captured authority, stable central-host/operation-key uniqueness, distinct stage evidence and an independent unknown-effect hold. A binary built before this increment, opening an upgraded database, either keeps working on the pre-existing mailbox data or refuses visibly without modifying or losing it; a test shows which, and the landing report states it, so that rollback to the kept previous build is safe.

Inert production store APIs durably admit one qualified operation before returning acceptance, return its recorded state for an exact duplicate, reject changed payload, command, target or captured authority for the same key, and enforce atomic bounded admission and payload limits before acceptance. Capacity pressure never evicts unresolved or settled deduplication evidence, including entries beyond the prompt-receipt display limit.

Deterministic tests through production store APIs cover concurrent duplicates, conflicting content, cuts before and after durable commit, a lost acceptance response and reopen/recovery without a second logical operation. Queue, runtime-accepted and processed evidence remain distinct; a mailbox ACK can be recorded without fabricated runtime acceptance and cannot clear an unknown runtime-effect hold. Actual process-crash coverage and any remaining integration crash cuts are explicitly identified rather than inferred from transaction rollback.

The increment exposes only inert journal/schema/store operations: no network dispatch, runtime execution, global queue resume, alternate-executor retry or new operator route is enabled. Its manifest pins the implementation base and the frozen prep source, lists the still-deferred M4 runtime/receipt/outage matrix, and states that this increment does not complete the M4 parent.

The focused prerequisite and production-store tests and the full five-stage gate pass on the final exact input; the independent read-only review pair has no outstanding in-scope Medium-or-higher finding, and independent acceptance evaluates this increment separately from the still-open M4 parent.
